tag_selection_notes: Tag 2.0.1 (or 2.0.0) is the optimal baseline target version. It contains representative vulnerable source code across major modules (e.g. default SECRET_KEY in config.py, sqla/models.py, views/core.py, tasks/slack_util.py, utils/core.py) prior to the 2.1.0/3.0.0 mitigation wave.

categories.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

cves.title: SQL Injection vulnerability in SQL Lab / Database connection queries
cves.description: SQL Injection issue allowing authenticated users with access to SQL Lab or dataset exploration to inject arbitrary SQL statements or bypass AST validation filters.

cves.title: SQL Injection in SQLLab via malicious Jinja templating
cves.description: Improper input validation in Jinja template processing allows crafted templates within SQL Lab queries to execute unauthorized SQL dialect commands.

cves.title: SQL Injection via improper query parameters in charts/views
cves.description: Improper neutralization in legacy chart and database parameter parsing leading to query parameter injection.

categories.name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

cves.title: Remote Code Execution via Celery task Slack integration parameter passing
cves.description: Unsanitized external notification hooks and Celery task payload processing that can lead to command injection or unauthorized process spawning.

cves.title: Unsafe deserialization of cached chart data or connection configuration
cves.description: Deserialization of untrusted payloads through caching backend or payload decompressors, leading to arbitrary code execution if backend cache is manipulated.

cves.title: SSRF in URL and asset import/export endpoints
cves.description: Internal network scanning and metadata retrieval via unvalidated database connection strings and URL fetching handlers.

cves.title: SSRF via database connection testing endpoints
cves.description: Missing network address validation allowing requests to internal network services via crafted database connection strings.

cves.title: Default Flask SECRET_KEY leading to session forgery and admin RCE
cves.description: Apache Superset installations defaulted to a known SECRET_KEY value, allowing unauthenticated attackers to forge session cookies with administrator privileges.

categories.name: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

cves.title: Stored XSS via dashboard markdown / title rendering
cves.description: Stored XSS triggered when an authenticated user crafts title or markdown metadata rendered without strict escaping to other users.

cves.title: Reflected XSS via error messages and query feedback
cves.description: Unescaped user input reflected in error responses or parameter validation dialogs.

cves.title: CSRF in state-changing endpoints without CSRF token enforcement
cves.description: Certain state-changing REST/JSON endpoints were exempt from CSRF token validation, enabling cross-site request exploitation.

categories.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor / Metadata Leak

cves.title: Sensitive database connection credential disclosure in error payloads
cves.description: Detailed error responses and tracebacks expose underlying database connection parameters, passwords, or internal metadata to non-admin users.

cves.title: Information disclosure via chart export / telemetry metadata
cves.description: Chart metadata endpoints leaked database schema and table structure information beyond the authenticated user's permissions.

cves.title: Improper query parameters parsing allowing access control bypass
cves.description: Inadequate parsing and validation of nested JSON query parameters leading to validation bypass and unauthorized data access.

categories.name: Insecure Default Initialization of Resource / Insecure Default Configuration

cves.title: Insecure default database engine specifications permitting arbitrary file reads / local connections
cves.description: Default engine specifications lacked restrictive sandbox flags, allowing SQLite and local connectors to read local files or connect to unauthorized sockets.
